svg.aria-label: The flow of discovery behind PLAN: each level that broke something, what it broke and the rule that came of it
svg.text: PLAN: the flow of discovery, Super Mario Bros. on the bench, 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-20
Each row is a level that broke something. Left: what broke. Right: the rule or tool that came out of it, kept from then on.
WHAT BROKE
WHAT IT TAUGHT
LEVEL
planner
A greedy walk hits the first goomba and cannot take
it back
Back up by segment: a move that dies is undone and the next best taken
planner
Enemy groups need timing; a pipe holds Mario past
the lookahead
Saved states (nes branch), a lookahead per move, a held segment is no
stall
planner
A gentler rule committed Mario to a gap
Keep a move only when a way on lives; keep the way on that found the
flag
planner
A castle has no flagpole
Done at the axe: $0770 turns 2, then the next world
planner
Water, and an exit pipe that puts Mario back
--swim (A tapped at measured rates); a pipe taken counts above x
bench
The grabber timed out before the intro frame
Grab at latches read off the bridge log, not on a clock
bench
A schedule larger than the head's room
The UNO's schedule became a ring: the head streams the rest during the
run
planner
The way on is up, and depth first cannot keep that
route alive
--beam: keep several positions a segment
bench
The console restarted itself mid-run with a clean
poll log
A part failure is not a plan failure: run it again, count only a clean
run
planner
A frame holding two polls played a jump one poll
late
The model stops on the poll, not at the frame's end
planner
The ceiling leads to a warp zone; the beam has no
room for height; a jump cannot keep A across a
segment
--beam-high, --no-ceiling, a warp is a death, A held as a way on,
--resume with .json sidecars; one stretch by hand
planner
A castle maze sends Mario back unless he stands at a
height as the screen reaches a page
The checks read out of the game's code; the loop-back a death; the
height slot aimed at the next check; one gap by hand
bench
Two polls seen in one look, the count starting at 1
Compare from the last reset line of the bridge log, not the last L 0
bench
A clean run with no frames: the grabber's limit was
shorter than the run
A limit set from the schedule's length
planner
The beam stood at the water's exit pipe for twenty
segments
A pipe passed stays passed: each position carries the pipes its own
path entered
planner
Checks that fire whatever Mario does, and the beam
stalled at x 1266 twice
Read in the code: the loop-back is a page shift under his feet,
progress once per check
planner
Counted every time, the beam circled a section four
times; a wrong pipe took it to page 1
A repeat of the same check is a death; a pipe that sets Mario back a
page in the loaded area is a trap
planner
A climb gains nothing to the right, so the beam
never strings it together
tools/plan-climb.py: a six-poll beam ranked by height, spliced on; the
water pipe's entry judged alive by $074F, not $0750
The end: one schedule of 1,752 button bytes, searched on the model level by level and played on the part from
power-on, run 20261020-192022: thirty-two levels, 77,402 polls checked against the script, none wrong, none
missing, no life lost. Twenty of the thirty-two levels taught nothing: the beam crossed them on its own.
Authored by tools/plan-discovery.py; the measured record is docs/plan-log.json and docs/plan-log.md.
